newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Weak machinery data to hit Swiss franc - CSFB. [CORRECTED 16:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Weak machinery data to hit Swiss franc - CSFB. [CORRECTED 16:40 GMT]

text.p: News that Swiss machinery orders fell 8.6 percent in 1996 and export orders (corrects to make clear that it was export orders that plunged and not exports themselves) plunged 14.6 percent in the fourth quarter bodes ill for the Swiss franc, which must fall more to avoid economic crisis, Credit Suisse First Boston said.

"Mark/Swiss franc will have some room to rise considerably in the next few weeks," it said in a forex trading strategy bulletin. "Last week's 87.75 top should already be taken out towards the end of this week."
CSFB cited the ASM/VSM machinery industry association's comment that the weak franc had not been able to counter economic weakness and price pressure in key export markets.
"This is very bad news for anyone who believes in economic stabilisation in 1997," it said.

It pointed out that machinery exports account for nearly 45 percent of Swiss goods exports, adding the steep drop in foreign orders in the second half of 1996 meant exports will slump again in the first half of 1997.

"With the domestic economy in an outright crisis, economic growth will again be negative in 1997, probably by far more than in 1996," it said. GDP, which has stagnated since 1990, is widely expected to have slipped around 0.6 percent in 1996.
"There is no other choice than a considerable further depreciation of the Swiss franc in order to prevent the economy from running into a full-fledged crisis."
